chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Isa, from his father, from Ali bin Nu'man, from Fudil bin Uthman, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and it was said to him: Indeed, these wicked ones narrate from your father, saying: Your father (peace be upon him) said: 'If you know, then do what you wish.' And hence, after that, they declare every forbidden thing permissible. He said: What is it with them, may Allah curse them? My father (peace be upon him) only said: 'If you know the truth, then do what you wish of goodness; it will be accepted from you.'

key_terms.الأخابث: The wicked ones (often referring to a specific sect like the Khawarij)
key_terms.الحق: The Truth (referring to divine truth or the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct interpretation of the Imam's saying 'If you know, then do what you wish'?
ai.summary: This narration from *Mani al-Akhbar* addresses the theological dispute regarding the principle of *al-Haqq* (the Truth) and its relationship to action, specifically countering the Khawarij or Mu'tazila who used the phrase to justify moral permissiveness (*istihlal*) after acquiring knowledge. Imam al-Baqir clarifies that 'knowing' refers to recognizing the Truth, which then permits one to freely choose and perform good deeds (*khayr*) that are accepted by God, rather than granting license for any action. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the integration of gnosis (*ma'rifah*) with righteous practice, ensuring that knowledge leads to voluntary obedience rather than arbitrary freedom.
